---
title: "Supplementary Figures"
subtitle: "A unified repertoire of indel mutational signatures in 6,975 tumors"
filters:
  - ../highlight.lua
  - at: post-render
    path: ../sup_fig_numbers.lua
crossref:
  fig-title: "Figure S"
  fig-prefix: "Figure S"
  title-delim: "."
format:
  html:
    toc: true
    embed-resources: true
    link-external-newwindow: true
  pdf:
    papersize: letter
    mainfont: TeX Gyre Pagella
    fig-pos: H
    geometry:
      - margin=0.75in
      - footskip=0.5in
    include-in-header:
      text: |
        \usepackage{lua-ul}
        \setcapindent{0pt}
        \setlength{\intextsep}{0pt}
        \setlength{\abovecaptionskip}{4pt}
        \setlength{\belowcaptionskip}{0pt}
    # crossref fig-title gives "Figure S 1" in LaTeX. Number the figures
    # "S1", "S2", ... instead (Quarto sets \figurename in the preamble, so
    # this has to come after it).
    include-before-body:
      text: |
        \renewcommand*\figurename{Figure}
        \renewcommand{\thefigure}{S\arabic{figure}}
---

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
# Warn at render time if any figure in sup_figs/ is older than one of its
# source plots in the code repository (mapping in sup_figures_manifest.tsv).
# The figures shown below are the cropped copies in sup_figs/cropped/, made
# by crop_sup_figs.sh at the top of the repository.
source(here::here("check_sup_figures.R"))
sup_figure_problems <- check_sup_figures(
  manifest = here::here("sup_figures_manifest.tsv"),
  sup_dir = here::here("sup_figs")
)
if (nrow(sup_figure_problems) > 0) {
  warning(
    "sup_figs/ possibly stale relative to the code repo:\n",
    paste0("  ", sup_figure_problems$file, ": ", sup_figure_problems$problem,
           collapse = "\n"),
    call. = FALSE, immediate. = TRUE
  )
}
```

::: {#fig-s1}
![](cropped/sup_fig_s1a.pdf){width=7in}

**Activities of 83- and 89-type mutational signatures across cancer
types**
:::

The size (radius) of each dot represents the proportion of genomes of
the given cancer type with activity of the signature. A dot is omitted
when 10% or fewer of the genomes have activity of the signature and the
mean is below 0.03 mutations per megabase. The color indicates the mean
number of mutations per megabase attributed to the signature, among the
genomes of that cancer type with activity of the signature. Only genomes
whose 83-type or 89-type signature assignment reconstructs the spectrum
with cosine similarity > 0.90 are included. A row labeled with an 83-type and an
89-type signature (for example C_ID4 / InsDel4) shows a pair with
identical activities. The figure continues on the next page.

{{< pagebreak >}}

![](cropped/sup_fig_s1b.pdf){width=7in fig-align="center"}

**Figure S1 (continued).**


{{< pagebreak >}}

<!-- Keep non-ASCII characters such as β out of caption titles. In a
caption they make LuaLaTeX report changed labels on every run, so the PDF
render stops at the maximum number of runs. -->

::: {#fig-s2}
![](cropped/sup_fig_s2ab.pdf){width=7in}

**Comparative mutational signatures across 83-, 89-, and 476-channel
classification of C_ID13 vs ID_C, C_ID11 vs C_ID16, and C_ID9 vs
ID_A**
:::

**(A)** Divergent sequence contexts for C_ID13 and ID_C. Top to bottom:
83-type, 89-type, and partial 476-type representations (1-bp C and T
deletions were displayed). While 89-type profiles exhibit high
similarity between the two signatures, the 476-type classification
reveals distinct flanking sequence preferences. Specifically, C_ID13
(InsDel13) demonstrates a predilection for ATTA and GTTA motifs, whereas
ID_C (InsDel_C) preferentially occurs at ATA and GTA contexts.

**(B)** Divergent sequence contexts for C_ID11 and C_ID16. Top to
bottom: 83-type, 89-type, and partial 476-type representations (1-bp C
and T insertions were displayed). While 89-type profiles exhibit high
similarity between the two signatures, the 476-type classification
reveals distinct flanking sequence preferences. Specifically, C_ID11
(InsDel11) exhibits a specific preference for 1-bp T insertions within
NTN motifs, while C_ID16 (InsDel16) shows a broader preference for NN
contexts. Panel C is on the next page.

{{< pagebreak >}}

![](cropped/sup_fig_s2c.pdf){width=7in fig-align="center"}

**Figure S2 (continued).**

**(C)** Divergent sequence contexts for C_ID9/InsDel9 and
ID_A/InsDel_Aβ. Top to bottom: 83-type, 89-type, and partial 476-type
representations (1-bp C and T deletions were displayed). Compared with
C_ID9, ID_A is nearly depleted of 1-bp T deletions. Although the
83-channel profiles show similar patterns of 1-bp C deletions, the 89-
and 476-channel classifications reveal distinct preferences for
flanking sequences. In particular, InsDel_Aβ preferentially exhibits
1-bp C deletions in TCA and TCT contexts.

{{< pagebreak >}}

::: {#fig-s3}
![](cropped/sup_fig_s3a.pdf){height=7.4in}

**83-type mutational signature asymmetries in transcription strands,
replication strands, and DNA regions across cancer types**
:::

**(A)** Transcription strand asymmetries of 83-type signatures. Each
row represents an 83-type signature, and each column represents a
cancer type. Red and dark blue circles indicate enrichment on the
transcribed and untranscribed strands, respectively. Significance of
enrichment is shown as stars (Fisher's exact test, \* p \< 0.05, \*\*
p \< 0.01, \*\*\* p \< 0.001). Color intensities and circle sizes
represent the odds ratio between the ratio of real mutations and the
ratio of simulated mutations (see Methods). Panels B and C are on the
next two pages.

{{< pagebreak >}}

![](cropped/sup_fig_s3b.pdf){height=7.4in fig-align="center"}

**Figure S3 (continued).**

**(B)** Replication strand asymmetries of 83-type signatures. Data are
presented as in panel A, with teal and salmon circles indicating
enrichment on the leading and lagging strands, respectively.

{{< pagebreak >}}

![](cropped/sup_fig_s3c.pdf){height=7.4in fig-align="center"}

**Figure S3 (continued).**

**(C)** Enrichment of mutations of 83-type signatures in genic and
intergenic regions. Data are presented as in panel A, with orange and
light blue circles indicating enrichment in genic and intergenic
regions, respectively.

{{< pagebreak >}}

::: {#fig-s4}
![](cropped/sup_fig_s4.pdf){width=7in}

**Interplay between 83-type signatures and replication time**
:::

Relative mutation counts of 83-type signatures per replication-timing
decile (y axes) are presented for early (left) to late (right)
replication domains. Real mutations are shown as bars, and simulated
mutations are shown as red dashed lines. Real and simulated counts are
each scaled to their own maximum, so the y axis shows the count relative
to the decile with the most mutations. The numbers above each plot are
the numbers of cancer types in which the signature increases, decreases,
or is flat from early to late replication. The trends are determined
separately for each cancer type and relative to the simulated mutations,
so they can differ from the pooled real counts shown as bars. Bars sum
the cancer types with a trend, that is, those with at least 500 real
indels attributed to the signature in which the real or the simulated
slope was significant. Green bars indicate signatures that increase from
early to late replication in every such cancer type. Yellow bars
indicate signatures that decrease in every such cancer type. Purple bars
indicate signatures that are flat (not affected by replication timing)
in more than half of them. Blue bars indicate all other signatures,
whose trends are inconsistent across cancer types.

{{< pagebreak >}}

::: {#fig-s5}
![](cropped/sup_fig_s5.pdf){width=7in}

**Mutational spectra of RNase H2-deficient murine tumors and RPE1 cell
clones**
:::

From top to bottom, spectra are displayed in 83-type, 89-type, and
partial 476-type representations (specifically highlighting ≥ 2-bp
deletions, ≥ 2-bp insertions, and deletions with microhomology).
Predominant peaks for ID_F/InsDel_F are evident in both RNase
H2-deficient tumors and RPE1 clones, characterized by Del:2bp:Repeats:2
and Del:2bp:MH:1 (83-type), L(2,8):U(1,2):R(2,4) and L(2,5):M1
(89-type), and Del2:U2:R2 and Del2:M1 (476-type). Notably, these
features are nearly absent in wild-type RPE1 control clones.


{{< pagebreak >}}

::: {#fig-s6}
![](cropped/sup_fig_s6.pdf){height=7.6in}

**Demographic associations of indel signatures with sex and age**
:::

**(A)** Sex association of 83-type and 89-type indel signatures. Bar
height represents the log₂ odds ratio (log₂OR), with positive values
indicating enrichment in females (red) and negative values indicating
enrichment in males (blue). Color shade indicates the significance
level (−log₁₀FDR, where FDR is the Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery
rate). Only signatures with FDR \< 0.2 are shown.

**(B)** Age association of 83-type and 89-type indel signatures across
cancer types. Color shade indicates the Spearman correlation
coefficient (ρ), and dot size corresponds to the significance level
(−log₁₀FDR). Only signatures with FDR \< 0.05 and ρ \> 0.1 are shown.
